title: Keep dynamically discovered provider error registries catchable
before: At first parent 1354e0bfa4847c1a71b9eea7374847a786d81c1b, the provider-error registry treated every exported name ending in "Error" as an exception and explicitly registered litellm.ErrorEventError. ErrorEventError was an ordinary class rather than a BaseException subclass, so the generated tuple could contain a non-catchable class. Runtime handlers using that tuple in an except clause could consequently raise TypeError instead of handling the provider exception.
after: At merge commit fb05748ace65bea780e0766b14b0904fbaac5f7f, discovery considers an "Error" export only when its object is a BaseException subclass, and the known non-exception ErrorEventError entry is removed from the configured registry. The tuple consumed by retry and reporting handlers therefore excludes that invalid member while retaining the configured provider exception classes.
diff: The change modifies aider/exceptions.py in two inseparable parts: it removes ExInfo("ErrorEventError", True, None) from EXCEPTIONS and strengthens the dynamic discovery predicate from a name-suffix check to `var.endswith("Error") and issubclass(getattr(litellm, var), BaseException)`. No test file changed. Existing tests construct the registry, inspect its tuple, and exercise a RateLimitError through a call site whose except clause consumes that tuple.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-discovered-error-types-by-catchability
candidate_atomics.title: Keep only catchable types in a dynamic error registry
candidate_atomics.description: Reconcile name-based provider error discovery and explicit metadata so the tuple supplied to language-level exception handlers contains only BaseException subclasses. The discovery guard and removal of the known invalid configured member form one operation because either change alone leaves a failure mode: filtering discovery alone does not remove an explicitly configured ordinary class, while pruning only the known class leaves future suffix-matching ordinary classes misclassified.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent provider request handlers from failing with a catch-clause TypeError caused by ordinary classes being included in a dynamically assembled exception tuple.
semantic_action.module_role: provider exception classification and retry-metadata registry
semantic_action.pre_state: Provider exports are classified by an error-like name alone, and at least one configured registry member is an ordinary class that cannot legally participate in an except tuple.
semantic_action.post_state: Discovered error-like exports must inherit from BaseException, and known ordinary classes are absent from the configured registry, so the produced handler tuple contains the intended catchable provider error types.
semantic_action.validation: Construct the registry, assert every emitted tuple member is a class derived from BaseException and the known ordinary error-like export is absent, then raise a later-listed provider exception through a real consumer's except tuple and verify metadata-driven handling occurs without TypeError. The checkout contains construction/tuple tests and a RateLimitError retry-path test, but no new explicit all-members-catchable assertion.
parameters: provider_module: runtime module whose exports are inspected
name_predicate: convention identifying candidate error exports
exception_base: BaseException or the language/runtime catchability root

candidate_workflows.name: repair-dynamic-provider-exception-registry
candidate_workflows.title: Repair a provider exception registry that admits non-catchable classes
candidate_workflows.description: Use when a provider adapter builds an exception-handling tuple from exported names and runtime handling fails because an error-like export is not an actual exception type. Establish catchability as the registry invariant, reconcile both discovery and explicit metadata, and validate through registry-level and real catch-path oracles.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a dynamically assembled provider exception registry can be safely used by retry and reporting handlers without changing their existing error-specific policies.
when_to_use: A runtime error reports that a class in an except clause does not inherit from the language's exception base.
A provider module exposes ordinary classes whose names satisfy the adapter's error-name convention.
An adapter constructs a catch tuple by combining provider-module discovery with an explicit metadata registry.
anti_goals: Do not classify an export as an exception solely because its name ends with an error-like suffix.
Do not add retry metadata for an ordinary provider payload or event class merely to satisfy a discovery-list consistency check.
Do not change retry decisions, user-facing descriptions, or handling semantics for valid provider exceptions unless separate evidence requires it.
Do not normalize provider error message or payload contents; this episode concerns exception-type classification and catchability.
not_applicable_when: The provider adapter receives only serialized error payloads and never constructs a language-level exception tuple.
All candidate registry values are already statically guaranteed to inherit from the runtime exception base.
The failure is caused by malformed provider payload fields rather than a non-catchable class in an exception registry.
inputs: The provider module or namespace inspected at runtime
The current explicit exception metadata registry
The runtime exception base class and catch semantics
Call sites that consume the generated exception tuple
Registry and request-path tests capable of exercising exception handling
workflow_graph.entry_state: An error-like naming convention and explicit registry can admit an ordinary class, and downstream request handlers consume the resulting classes directly in except clauses.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Discovery admits only catchable exception subclasses, explicitly configured non-exception entries are removed, valid exception metadata remains intact, and representative consumers can catch and process a provider exception without a catch-clause TypeError.

steps.condition: Apply when inspection establishes that name-based discovery or explicit metadata includes a type that is not derived from the runtime exception base.
steps.validation: Verify the registry's emitted tuple contains only BaseException subclasses and excludes the identified ordinary class; then exercise a consumer with a representative provider exception whose handling consults retry metadata.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm discovery combines the naming convention with a catchability/subclass predicate and the known invalid explicit entry is absent.
Registry check: instantiate the adapter and assert the emitted exception tuple is nonempty and every member is a BaseException subclass.
Focused regression check: assert the identified ordinary error-like export is not present in the emitted tuple.
Consumer check: raise a representative provider exception through a retry or reporting call site and verify normal metadata-driven handling occurs without TypeError.
Project check: run the focused exception and send-chat test modules in the pinned dependency environment.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the allegedly invalid provider export cannot be inspected or its inheritance relationship cannot be established.
Stop if consumers do not use the registry in language-level exception handling; this workflow would address the wrong boundary.
Do not claim complete validation if only registry construction is tested and no catch path or all-members-catchable assertion is available.
Stop and investigate separately if subclass inspection itself encounters non-class exports matching the name convention, because the pinned implementation assumes such matching exports are classes.
unresolved_or_deferred: No test was added by PR #4748 that directly asserts every tuple member inherits from BaseException or that ErrorEventError is absent.
The supplied bundle contains no CI/status-check results, and tests were not executed during this extraction because the checkout environment lacks the pinned runtime dependency.
The implementation calls issubclass directly after name matching; behavior for a matching non-class export is not covered by the change or tests.

The supplied routing label mentions provider error payload normalization, but the checkout evidence supports the narrower reusable capability of provider exception-type normalization and catchability enforcement.

unresolved_questions: Were the existing exception and send-chat tests executed successfully for PR #4748? Status-check metadata is unavailable in the supplied bundle.

Does the supported provider namespace guarantee that every export ending in "Error" is a class? If not, an `isinstance(candidate, type)` guard may be needed before issubclass, but this episode contains no evidence of such a failure.

A direct regression assertion for exclusion of ordinary error-like classes is absent, so validation strength is limited to the implementation diff, existing registry tests, and an existing consumer catch-path test.

title: Reject runtime wrapper instances as provider error bodies
before: At parent commit 66cd061ab468aeae9fd2e38715d3931f7f77f569, provider error normalization treated every non-null object with enumerable keys as a usable body. Node-style streams with a pipe method were excluded, but class instances and wrapper objects without pipe were JSON-serialized. Downstream formatting could then select serialized implementation internals instead of the diagnostic Error.message.
after: At commit 4523528b21c66084fdece7ed3ffa10888bc5ac60, object-valued body candidates are accepted only when non-empty and their prototype is Object.prototype or null. Class instances and response wrappers are rejected, leaving body undefined so downstream formatting preserves Error.message; strings and plain parsed JSON objects remain supported.
diff: The change replaced isNonEmptyObject with isPlainNonEmptyObject for both the nested error field and response-body field. The new predicate checks value type, null, prototype identity, and enumerable-key count. Three regression tests cover rejection of a response-body class instance, rejection of a nested-error class instance, and continued serialization of a plain parsed JSON object. No provider call sites or formatter branches were changed.

commit.subject: fix(ai): treat only plain objects as provider error bodies (#7205)
commit.body_excerpt:
pickBodyText serialized any non-empty object into the error body. SDK error
fields can hold class instances instead of parsed bodies - AWS SDK v3's
$response.body is an HTTP stream/response wrapper - and stringifying one
produced garbage like {"_events":...} as the body, which then replaced
error.message in the composed display string. error.message is where the SDK
puts the real deserialized exception text ("Input is too long...", schema
validation details), so the one useful string was discarded for noise.

The existing pipe-based stream sniffing only covers node-style streams; web
ReadableStreams (pipeTo/pipeThrough, no pipe) and non-stream wrapper classes
slipped through. Require Object.prototype/null prototype before serializing
a candidate body - parsed JSON bodies are plain objects by construction, so
real gateway bodies still surface.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned change replaces both generic non-empty-object checks with a plain-object predicate that accepts only Object.prototype or null prototypes and still requires at least one enumerable key.
After the change, string bodies remain directly usable, pipe-like response streams remain excluded, class-instance object bodies are rejected, and non-empty plain objects remain JSON-serialized.
The normalized result controls displayed provider failures: the shared formatter uses Error.message whenever no accepted body exists, while otherwise it may format status and body.
The Bedrock error adapter explicitly chooses normalized status and body only when messageCarriesBody is false and both values exist; otherwise it uses the normalized message.

At the pinned ref, the shared normalizer or formatter is used by Bedrock, OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI, Google, and image-provider error paths, so the classification boundary is shared across multiple adapters.
A regression test supplies a response-body class instance without a pipe method and asserts that no body is extracted, the useful 'Input is too long' message remains, and messageCarriesBody is true.
A regression test supplies a class instance in the nested error field and asserts that it is not serialized and that 'TLS handshake failed' remains the normalized message.
A compatibility test supplies a non-empty plain parsed JSON body and asserts that it is still serialized and marked as separate from the opaque SDK message.
The added assertions jointly define the validation oracle: reject non-plain runtime objects from both supported object-valued slots while continuing to surface legitimate plain structured payloads.

candidate_workflows.name: normalize-ambiguous-provider-error-object-payloads
candidate_workflows.title: Normalize ambiguous object-valued provider error payloads without losing diagnostics
candidate_workflows.description: Tighten a shared error-normalization boundary when SDK fields may contain either parsed payloads or runtime wrapper instances. Establish the accepted structured-body shape, apply it consistently to every object-valued candidate slot, and validate both rejection and compatibility behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure displayed provider failures use genuine structured payloads when available and otherwise preserve the useful diagnostic message instead of serialized SDK or transport internals.
when_to_use: A provider or transport SDK stores heterogeneous values in fields treated as error bodies.
Displayed errors contain serialized wrapper internals or stream state instead of the exception message.
Existing filtering recognizes only a specific runtime capability, such as a pipe method, and misses other class-based wrappers.
anti_goals: Do not remove support for string error bodies.
Do not suppress non-empty plain parsed JSON payloads merely because they are object-valued.
Do not redesign provider-specific call sites or error-message prefixes when the defect is in the shared payload-admission boundary.
Do not infer body legitimacy from serializability or enumerable keys alone.
not_applicable_when: The candidate payload is already governed by a reliable typed or schema-validated body contract.
The error corruption occurs after normalization and is unrelated to selecting an object-valued body.
The runtime value must intentionally support custom-prototype records as documented payloads; this exact plain-object rule would require a different compatibility contract.
inputs: Representative failing error containing a runtime wrapper or class instance
The object-valued fields probed as possible bodies
The fallback diagnostic message that must survive rejection
Representative legitimate string and plain structured bodies
Downstream formatter behavior when normalized body is absent or present

commit.subject: fix(logging): show HTTP status code and 400 body in API error output (#3096)
commit.body_excerpt:
When an API call fails, the terminal output now includes the HTTP status
code in the header line and, for 400 errors, the response body from the
provider (truncated to 300 chars). Makes it much easier to diagnose
issues like invalid model names or malformed requests that were
previously hidden behind generic error messages.

Salvaged from PR #2646 by Mibayy. Fixes #2644.

title: Normalize byte-encoded API error response bodies as UTF-8 without altering unrecognized payloads
before: At parent 96cc8a0daddd1e66597ff862be20434a5d6a1b1b, the error adapter only handled response.data when it was a comma-containing string. It converted every numeric-looking element with String.fromCharCode, so it did not handle Uint8Array/Buffer payloads, interpreted UTF-8 bytes as independent UTF-16 code units, and accepted numeric values outside the byte range. Non-comma strings and strings containing non-numeric elements were left unchanged.
after: At 69bf2d75efda831957172668d0b7e50c14fc0214, the adapter recognizes raw Uint8Array values (including Buffer subclasses) and valid comma-separated integer byte strings, decodes both through TextDecoder as UTF-8, and mutates response.data before API-error logging and rethrow. Comma-separated strings are normalized only when every value is an integer from 0 through 255; ordinary strings, non-numeric sequences, and out-of-range sequences remain unchanged.
diff: The change replaces String.fromCharCode conversion with byte-oriented UTF-8 decoding, adds a direct Uint8Array branch, and adds integer/range validation before constructing a Uint8Array from serialized bytes. Existing normalization call sites remain in the non-streaming request rejection path and the streaming-request setup rejection path. Tests add coverage for raw Uint8Array data, two-byte and three-byte UTF-8 text, and out-of-range preservation while retaining prior ASCII, ordinary-string, and malformed-string cases.

Comma-separated strings are normalized only when every value is an integer from 0 through 255; ordinary strings, non-numeric sequences, and out-of-range sequences remain unchanged.
episode.diff: The change replaces String.fromCharCode conversion with byte-oriented UTF-8 decoding, adds a direct Uint8Array branch, and adds integer/range validation before constructing a Uint8Array from serialized bytes. Existing normalization call sites remain in the non-streaming request rejection path and the streaming-request setup rejection path. Tests add coverage for raw Uint8Array data, two-byte and three-byte UTF-8 text, and out-of-range preservation while retaining prior ASCII, ordinary-string, and malformed-string cases.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 69bf2d75efda831957172668d0b7e50c14fc0214 is a single-parent implementation commit for PR/issue 23341 and changes the error adapter plus its tests.

The parent implementation only examines comma-containing strings, maps their elements with Number, accepts them when none is NaN, and converts them with String.fromCharCode; it has no raw Uint8Array branch or byte-range check.
The implementation adds direct Uint8Array decoding, validates serialized values as integers in the inclusive 0-255 range, and decodes the resulting bytes using TextDecoder.

The resulting adapter navigates only object-shaped errors with a response.data field; Uint8Array data is decoded directly, while comma-separated strings are decoded only after every parsed element satisfies the byte-domain predicate.
When a non-streaming content request rejects, normalization runs before API-error logging and the same error object is then rethrown.
When creation of a streaming request rejects before returning an async generator, normalization likewise runs before logging and rethrow.
A rejected request carrying response.data as Uint8Array([72,101,108,108,111]) is asserted to rethrow with response.data normalized to "Hello".
Serialized byte strings are asserted to decode multi-byte UTF-8 correctly for both "Héllo" and the three-byte-per-character text "こんにちは".
A serialized sequence containing 256 is asserted to remain unchanged rather than being coerced into a byte array.
Regression cases assert that ASCII serialized bytes still decode to "Hello", an ordinary error message remains unchanged, and a sequence containing a non-numeric element remains unchanged.

The added tests exercise the public generateContent rejection path and inspect the rethrown error object's response.data, providing an oracle for both successful normalization and preservation behavior; the available checkout has all tracked files deleted from the working tree, so this extraction did not execute the test suite.

candidate_atomics.title: Decode recognized error bytes as UTF-8 text
candidate_atomics.description: Convert either a raw byte array or a validated serialized byte sequence into readable UTF-8 text before downstream error handling observes the response body.

candidate_workflows.name: normalize-provider-error-byte-payload
candidate_workflows.title: Normalize byte-encoded provider errors before logging and propagation
candidate_workflows.description: At the provider failure boundary, conservatively identify supported byte payloads, decode them as UTF-8, and preserve the surrounding error flow and unsupported payloads.

workflow_graph.goal: Make byte-encoded provider error bodies readable across raw and serialized transport forms without corrupting unrelated data or changing rejection semantics.
when_to_use: A provider client sometimes exposes an error response body as a byte array or as comma-separated numeric bytes.
Multi-byte UTF-8 text is currently mojibake because byte values are converted directly to characters.
Normalization can run at a shared failure boundary before logging and propagation.
anti_goals: Do not rewrite ordinary textual or structured error payloads.
Do not accept fractional, negative, non-numeric, or greater-than-255 values as bytes.
Do not swallow, replace, or convert the original request rejection into success.
Do not redesign telemetry, retry behavior, authentication handling, or provider request routing.
not_applicable_when: The payload is already reliable text or structured data and no byte transport representation is observed.
The transport uses an encoding other than UTF-8 and its encoding contract is unknown.
The failure bypasses the adapter's request-rejection boundary, such as an error raised later while consuming an already-created stream.
inputs: provider request error object
response-body field to inspect
supported raw byte-array runtime type
serialized-byte syntax
UTF-8 decoder
existing error logging and rethrow boundary
workflow_graph.entry_state: A provider request has failed, and downstream logging or callers may observe an unreadable, byte-shaped response body.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Supported byte representations have become readable UTF-8 text before logging and rethrow; unsupported values are unchanged and the original failure still propagates.

steps.condition: The failed request exposes a response-body field.
steps.validation: Confirm raw byte arrays are admitted, serialized values are admitted only when every element is an integer from 0 through 255, and ordinary or invalid inputs remain unchanged.

steps.condition: The response body was recognized as a supported byte representation.
steps.validation: Confirm exact decoding of ASCII, two-byte UTF-8, and three-byte UTF-8 examples through the public rejection path, then confirm the normalized error is still rethrown.

validation_ladder: Unit-check admission and preservation boundaries with ordinary text, malformed serialized values, and out-of-range values.
Unit-check raw byte-array decoding with a known ASCII payload.
Unit-check serialized multi-byte UTF-8 decoding with both two-byte and three-byte characters.
Integration-check the request rejection boundary: normalization occurs before error logging and the original error object remains rejected/rethrown.
Separately verify every provider failure path that should share the contract, including stream creation and any errors raised during stream iteration.
stop_conditions: Stop if the response object or response-body field cannot be established from runtime evidence.
Stop and preserve the payload if serialized elements are not all integral bytes in the inclusive 0-255 range.
Defer decoding when the transport encoding is not known to be UTF-8.
Do not claim completion for failure paths that do not invoke the normalization boundary.
unresolved_or_deferred: The change calls normalization for non-streaming request rejection and streaming-request creation rejection, but the shown stream-iteration catch logs and rethrows without invoking the adapter.
Tests directly cover the non-streaming generateContent rejection path; no added test demonstrates the streaming-request setup call site.

The test suite was not executed because the provided working tree contains only .git with tracked files staged as deleted; validation claims are therefore based on committed test code, not a fresh run.
TextDecoder's default replacement behavior for malformed UTF-8 byte sequences is not explicitly tested or configured as fatal.

unresolved_questions: Should errors raised while consuming an already-created response stream receive the same response-body normalization as initial request and stream-creation failures?
Is replacement-character decoding acceptable for malformed UTF-8, or should decoding reject and preserve the original payload?
The committed tests establish source-level validation oracles, but a clean checkout is needed to execute them and confirm runtime validation.
